risks.note: Management states the Company has taken bold steps 'to remain competitive and to ensure survival by reducing cost and streamlining the overall operations process' and concedes 'severe competition and reduced demand', with optimism resting only on mid- and long-term prospects. Competitive intensity therefore bears directly on volumes and pricing.
risks.risk: Severe competition and reduced demand in the electrical equipment market

risks.note: Explicitly flagged in MD&A: 'The availability and cost of the funds remain very important factors impacting on the plans of the Company and threatening the viability itself.' This is the one risk management raises to the level of a viability concern, and it constrains the ability to fund product expansion and working capital for the order book.

MD&A states segment-wise performance 'is not applicable to the Company as there is only one identified reportable segment'. All revenue depends on one electrical-equipment business with no diversifying cash flow, so a downturn in that market flows through undamped.

The cautionary statement names 'availability of critical materials and their cost' among the important factors that could influence operations, alongside 'domestic demand and supply conditions affecting selling prices' - i.e. input costs may not be passable into prices.
risks.risk: Input availability and cost of critical materials

risks.note: Named in the cautionary statement as a factor influencing operations; industry capacity additions in a commoditising electrical-equipment market pressure realisations for a small manufacturer.
risks.risk: New capacity additions by the industry and domestic demand/supply conditions affecting selling prices

risks.note: Named in the cautionary statement as a factor material to business operations. The Company's own outlook is explicitly premised on government structural reforms and initiatives (ease of doing business, Digital India, Make in India), so policy direction is a two-sided exposure.
risks.risk: Changes in government policies and tax laws

risks.note: Form AOC-2 discloses an ongoing sale/purchase/supply arrangement with Jyoti Limited, a Promoter Group Company, valued at Rs. 564.30 Lakhs for April 2025-March 2026, covering starters, motors, instrument transformers, control panels and spares, plus trade mark usage and service charges disclosed in the Ind AS 24 note. A material slice of trade and the brand right therefore sit with a promoter-group counterparty rather than at arm's length in the open market.
risks.risk: Dependence on promoter-group related parties for trade

risks.note: The auditor's Emphasis of Matter records that management decided from 1 April 2025 to hold the quoted equity shares of Jyoti Limited for the long term, moving them from FVTPL to FVTOCI-NR under Ind AS 109 - a reclassification that 'cannot be revoked in future', with comparatives not restated. Reported fair market value on the reporting date was INR 527.67 lakhs and the change reduced income by INR 346.55 lakhs (gross) during the year. Reported earnings are thus exposed to, and now permanently insulated from, movements in a single promoter-group listed holding, and the ratio changes disclosed in MD&A are attributed to this same reclassification rather than to trading performance.
risks.risk: Concentration in, and irrevocable reclassification of, the quoted equity investment in Jyoti Limited

sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).
